questions.prompt: How should the TUI be invoked?
questions.description: Currently `notebooklm` is the main CLI, with `notebooklm-mcp` and `notebooklm-server` as separate entry points.

questions.prompt: Which CLI command groups should be accessible from the TUI?
questions.description: The full CLI has: notebook, source, artifact, chat, generate, download, label, note, collection, research, skill, share, language, profile, doctor, agent, session.
questions.recommendedAnswer: notebook, source, artifact, chat, generate, download

questions.prompt: What layout structure do you want?
questions.description: The reference pattern uses a fixed grid with header, content panes, and footer. Pick the general arrangement.

options.label: Header + Sidebar | Main | Detail panel | Footer

questions.description: This is the navigation/discovery pane on the left.

options.label: Hybrid: notebooks at top, commands at bottom

questions.prompt: What interaction model for the main content area?
questions.description: How does the user navigate and trigger actions?

options.label: Vim-like: j/k navigate, Enter selects, : for commands (Recommended)
Tab cycles panes, arrows navigate, Enter activates
Click to select, scroll, with keyboard fallback

questions.prompt: How should chat work in the TUI?
questions.description: Chat is conversational and might need special treatment.

options.label: Inline input bar at bottom, messages scroll in main pane (Recommended)
Dedicated fullscreen chat view (toggle with key)
Inline input + fullscreen toggle for long conversations

questions.prompt: For long-running operations (generate, download), how should the TUI handle them?
questions.description: The reference pattern suggests background threads with animated spinners.

options.label: Background thread with spinner + progress bar in footer (Recommended)
asyncio event loop integration (most complex, most responsive)

questions.prompt: What should the TUI show on launch?

options.label: Dashboard: notebook count, recent activity, profile info (Recommended)

questions.description: The reference mentions a centralized theme dictionary with bezel definitions.
